title: How can I make game assets with AI
author: aslan-trager1
selftext: Hi everyone, hope you’re all doing well imm curious how you use AI to make game assets that stay consistent with the same art style what tools or workflow do you use?

comments.author: Runner5964
comments.body: I know of two ways that work for me but I am a newbie myself. 1) Create an Image in ChatGPT or whatever of all your Game Assets and then give it to Claude to model them in blender (a good reference picture is important) 2) Tripo

replies.author: aslan-trager1
replies.body: Thanks im gonna try both ways

replies.author: Runner5964
replies.body: Sure, for the first way it is recommended to tell chatGPT exactly what you want in the reference images. Ideally you should have all sides of the asset (you can do that in one picture) and a plain background. Also the art style should be described exactly the same for all images

replies.author: watts320
replies.body: Is there a reason you use Claude to model them in blender? Is it better at doing that then chatgpt?

replies.author: PettyPotatoJuror
replies.body: I use the Chat GPT Codex App with the blender MCP and Tripo (although I use studio and not the API). Codex (Astra/Sol) and Claude can both build in blender, but you'll need multiple passes. Tripo is a good looking result faster but will require cleanup in blender (which is another task both Claude and Codex can handle fairly well).

comments.author: No-Dragonfruit-675
comments.body:
The best way is to create anchor reference images. For a character, can create a character sheet and forward feed that into downstream generation (3D model gen, 2D sprite sheets, etc...)

https://i.redd.it/kbtniin9ag0i1.png

Create a nice re-usable base prompt that explains what a character sheet should look like.

replies.author: aslan-trager1
replies.body: Thanks looks like referance images currently best way to do it.

replies.author: kbone213
replies.body: Can you share your workflow for that? I'm guessing comfyui.

comments.author: KorterArcade
comments.body: Build a pipeline. Make a materials studio with all your textures and patterns. This requires no images. All math driven. Then build an asset generator. This will be better to build consistent models that look like they belong in the same world. Build the generators to include the textures, uv, LOD, and seeds for models that you need. These can both be blender add ons build to export to your game engine

replies.author: Fair_One6452
replies.body: I read your comment, I new to game creation. What is thevprocess to built that asset generator? Im new to AI also, and learning about GitHub. So if you could add some more context that would be so appreciated. Before I just had ChatGPT create Sprite sheets. But a pipeline sounds better. Thank you in advance.

comments.author: TennDevStudios
comments.body: Codex with Astra model can do a pretty good job as long as you provide examples and judge its attempts and tell it what is wrong when it messes up.  Make it create tools to check for consistency and correct itself when it deviates, and have it make proper Skills for character generation and animations.   It takes a bit of back and forth to get a proper set up, but once it has the recipe and does it to your satisfaction it can pump out repeatable consistent sprites for 2D.   You just need to train it and force it to record its lessons and processes on what worked and what didn't work until you are getting outputs you're happy with.

comments.author: TheSpriteWizard
comments.body: Which style are you going for? If you want isometric I have a free tool for you. https://thespritewizard.itch.io/sprite-forge-kanes-character-creator

replies.author: aslan-trager1
replies.body: Thanks! I haven't fully locked in a style yet, still experimenting. Isometric could work though, so I'll give your tool a try. Out of curiosity, what's your workflow for keeping everything looking consistent once you've picked a style?

replies.author: TheSpriteWizard
replies.body: I make sure my workflow follows the art style. Making sprites can be tough, so using preexisting tools helps a lot.

comments.author: Flock_OfBirds
comments.body: Install the Spritulus MCP https://spritulus.com/mcp and it can produce cartoon-like characters, parallax backgrounds, nine slices, tile maps, etc.

replies.author: Flock_OfBirds
replies.body: You can also just use that site with AI and ave yourself big time on token costs.

comments.author: getloadoutai
comments.body: Id make a tiny reference sheet first: palette, proportions, outlines, lighting and camera angle. then test three different assets together in the actual game, a consistent prompt helps but doesnt guarantee a consistent style. easier to catch the drift on three assets than after generating 80 things that look like they belong to different games
